description: Everything the capture window is allowed to do. Nothing is permitted by default in Tauri v2 — if it is not listed here, the frontend cannot call it. Two things here are easy to get wrong, so both are pinned by tests in src-tauri/src/capabilities.rs. (1) plugin-fs permissions are strictly PER-COMMAND: fs:allow-read-file buys read_file and nothing else, so every command src/app/files.ts calls needs its own entry. (2) fs:scope grants no command at all — it only widens the global scope those entries are checked against, which is how the app-data and scratch dirs get declared once instead of nine times. NO entry here carries a scope of its own: the static scope is exactly $APPDATA and Quacket's own $TEMP/quacket, for reads and writes alike. The two paths that legitimately point outside it are both earned at RUNTIME, per file, rather than pre-granted as a glob — plugin-dialog allows a picked path inside its own command, and src-tauri/src/dnd.rs allows a dropped image the moment it is dropped. That is why fs:allow-read-file needs no wide scope; it used to claim $HOME/** 'for the arbitrary path the user picked', which was both a blanket grant over everything the user owns AND still too narrow to open a screenshot on a second drive. There is no shell permission: Quacket spawns through its own quacket_run / quacket_spawn commands, whose allowlist lives in src-tauri/src/proc.rs.
